This appeal coming on for orders this day, the court  following:
 JUDGEMENT Heard finally, with the consent of the parties.

2] This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 06.02.2020,
passed by Fourth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.3518/2017 whereby, a sum of Rs.19,19,965/- has been awarded to the appellants on account of death of Balraj Yadav.

3] In brief, the facts of the case are that deceased Balraj Yadav met with an accident on 12.07.2017, when he was driving his auto bearing registration No.MP-11-R-0424, and was going towards Dhar, at that time, a trailer bearing registration No.MP- 09-KD-9289, being driven rashly and negligently by the respondent No.1, dashed against the auto of Balraj, which resulted in grievous injuries caused to him.

Balraj was taken to Government Bhoj Hospital, Dhar,
and from there, he was shifted to Gokuldas Hospital, however, while being treated, he died on 24.07.2017.

Subsequently, a claim case was filed by the appellants, as appellant No.1, being the wife of Balraj, and appellant Nos.2 & 3 being his parents, whereas appellant No.4 being the minor daughter of the deceased.
The learned Member of the MACT, after recording the evidence, has awarded the compensation as aforesaid, and being aggrieved of the inadequacy of the same, this appeal has been preferred.

4] Counsel for the appellants has submitted that the award is on the lower side, especially the income of the deceased assessed by the MACT to be Rs.8,435/-, despite the fact that the deceased was having an auto rickshaw of his own, and had also obtained a loan for the same.
It is also submitted that towards consortium also, only Rs.40,000/- has been awarded to the appellant No.1 only.
It is further submitted that towards loss of estate also, no amount has been awarded.

5] Counsel for the respondent No.3, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted Smt. Hemlata vs Ranjeet Yadav on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157719649/

2 that no case for interference is made out as the appellants have not been able to prove that the deceased was having an auto rickshaw and had taken a loan for the same.
6] Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7] From the record, it is found that so far as the income of the deceased is concerned, the Tribunal has come to a conclusion that the income of the deceased can be considered as that of a skilled labour, to be Rs.8,435/- p.m., as per the Government guidelines of 2017.
It was also found that the appellants have not been able to prove that the deceased owned an auto rickshaw, or that he also obtained a loan from the bank.

In such circumstances, although the contention of the appellants cannot be accepted, however, considering that fact that the license of the deceased has been proved, and he was already maintaining a family of five persons, this Court is of the opinion that instead of Rs.8,435/-, his income ought to have been considered as Rs.9,000/- p.m., and it is also found that towards consortium, only Rs.40,000/- has been awarded, instead of Rs.40,000/- to each of the appellants.
So far as the loss of estate is concerned, it is also found that no compensation has been awarded towards the aforesaid head.

In such circumstances, the assessment of compensation can be made in the following manner vis-a-vis,
the assessment made by the Claims Tribunal:-

The assessment made by the claims Tribunal:-
 Dependency 7873 X 12 X 16 15,11,616/-
 Amount awarded in the other heads  Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 Consortium 40,000/-
 Medical expenses 3,53,349/-
 Total 19,19,965/-
The assessment made by this Court is as under :-
Dependency 9000 + 40% (3600/-) = 16,12,800/-
 12,600 X 12=1,51,200/- x 1/3 = 50,400 X  16 =
 Amount awarded in other heads by the  Tribunal  Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 Consortium 1,60,00  Medical expenses 3,53,34  Loss of estate 15,000

3  Total 21,56,14  Amount awarded by the Tribunal - 19,19,9  Amount to be enhanced 2,36,18  8] In view of the above, the appeal stands partly al the appellants shall be entitled to receive an additional enhanced amount of Rs.2,36,184/- towards the compensation along with the interest as awarded by the Tribunal.
